patient_profile.name: Patient E
history: received childhood vaccinations, but missed recent meningococcal booster
patient_profile.presenting_complaint: severe, throbbing headache, high fever, and stiff neck starting 12 hours ago, with extreme sensitivity to light

hidden_ground_truth.stage: Acute phase, rapidly progressive; patient is at high risk of sepsis, DIC, and neurological injury
hidden_ground_truth.correct_first_line_treatment: Blood cultures followed immediately by empiric IV antibiotics (Ceftriaxone 2g + Vancomycin 15-20mg/kg) and IV Dexamethasone (10mg) administered prior to or with the first dose of antibiotics. Lumbar puncture should be performed immediately unless there are focal neuro signs warranting a head CT first, but antibiotics must not be delayed for imaging.
red_herrings: history of a mild head bump 2 days ago (which the patient attributes her headache to initially)

initial: severe headache, rated 10/10, constant, worse with any movement
neck stiffness and discomfort when trying to bend neck

on_direct_questioning.head_bump: I bumped my head on a shelf 2 days ago. It left a tiny bruise but didn't hurt much. This headache is completely different, like my head is going to explode.
on_direct_questioning.focal_weakness: No weakness in my arms or legs, and no numbness.
on_direct_questioning.rash: I think I saw a few small purple spots on my legs this morning, but I thought they were just minor bruises.
on_direct_questioning.kernig_sign: positive (pain and resistance when extending the knee with hip flexed)
on_direct_questioning.brudzinski_sign: positive (flexing the neck causes the patient to flex her knees and hips)

csf_analysis.glucose: 18 mg/dL (very low; blood glucose is 100 mg/dL)

lab_results.ct_head: no midline shift, no mass effect, no evidence of increased intracranial pressure contraindicating lumbar puncture

progression_rules.if_untreated_or_delayed: progresses rapidly to altered mental status, seizures, purpura fulminans, septic shock, or death within hours
progression_rules.if_correct_treatment: systemic symptoms and headache gradually improve over 24-48 hours with appropriate IV antibiotics
progression_rules.if_incorrect_or_unnecessary_treatment: e.g. treating as migraine or concussion, or holding antibiotics to wait for head CT / CSF culture results, delays life-saving therapy and results in clinical deterioration
progression_rules.if_unnecessary_invasive_test_ordered: simulate normal/expected result, note added delay in scoring
